---
title: "gtExtras"
output: html_notebook
---

Pre-requisites

```{r}
library('tidyverse')
library('gtExtras')
```

```{r}
data("mtcars")
print(mtcars)
```

Let's print our table in a colorful manner

```{r}
head(mtcars) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
  tab_header(title = "Table Styled like Guardian")

```

Hulk data_color

```{r}
head(mtcars) %>% 
  gt::gt() %>% 
  gt_hulk_col_numeric(mpg)
```

Let's use multiple columns

```{r}
head(mtcars) %>% 
  gt::gt() %>% 
  gt_hulk_col_numeric(mpg:wt,trim = TRUE)
```

The color pallete ranges from purple which is low to green which is the highest

We can reverse the color Palette by using reverse function

```{r}
head(mtcars) %>% 
  gt::gt() %>% 
  gt_hulk_col_numeric(mpg:disp,reverse = TRUE,trim = TRUE)
```

Now using gt_color_rows

The [`gt_color_rows()`](https://jthomasmock.github.io/gtExtras/reference/gt_color_rows.html) function is a more generic, thin boilerplate wrapper around [`gt::data_color()`](https://gt.rstudio.com/reference/data_color.html). A quick example of [`gt::data_color()`](https://gt.rstudio.com/reference/data_color.html) is below.

Using named colors or hex colors is very simple!

```{r}
head(mtcars) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt::data_color(
    columns = mpg:disp,colors = c('white','purple')
  )
```

Using a blue pallette for our data

```{r}
mtcars %>% 
  head() %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_color_rows(mpg:disp,palette = "ggsci::blue_material")
```

Highlighting Rows

```{r}
 head_car <- head(mtcars) %>%
  rownames_to_column("cars")
```

```{r}
names(head_car)
```

```{r}
gt(head_car) %>%
  gt_theme_nytimes() %>% 
  gt_highlight_rows(rows = 2,font_weight = 'bold')
```

We may want to only need to bolden the target column and just highlight the rest this is how we do this

```{r}
gt(head_car) %>% 
  gt_theme_nytimes() %>% 
  gt_highlight_rows(rows = 5 , bold_target_only = TRUE,target_col = cars,fill= 'grey')
```

Plotting with gtExtras

Data Preparation

```{r}
 mtcars %>% 
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  summarise(mpg_data = list(mpg)) %>% 
  print()
```

1)  gt_sparkline( )

```{r}
mtcars %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
   # must end up with list of data for each row in the input dataframe
  summarize(mpg_data = list(mpg), .groups = "drop") %>%
   gt() %>%
   gt_plt_sparkline(mpg_data)
```

2)  gt_plt_dist()

plotting Distributions of our data

```{r}
mtcars %>% 
  group_by(cyl) %>% 
  summarize(mpg_data = list(mpg), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_nytimes() %>% 
  gt_plt_dist(mpg_data)
```

3)gt_bar_plot

```{r}
mtcars %>% 
  head() %>%
  select(cyl,mpg) %>% 
  mutate(mpg_pct_max = round(mpg/max(mpg) * 100 , 2),
         mpg_scaled = mpg/max(mpg) * 100) %>% 
  mutate(mpg_uncscaled = mpg) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_nytimes() %>% 
  gt_plt_bar_pct(column = mpg_scaled , scaled = TRUE,fill = "green",background = 'lightgreen') %>% 
  gt_plt_bar_pct(column = mpg_uncscaled, scaled = FALSE,fill = "darkblue",background = 'lightblue')
```

```{r}
team_df <- readRDS(url("https://github.com/nflverse/nflfastR-data/raw/master/teams_colors_logos.rds"))

team_df %>%
  dplyr::select(team_nick, team_abbr, team_conf, team_division, team_wordmark) %>%
  head(8) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "team_conf") %>%
  gt_merge_stack(col1 = team_nick, col2 = team_division) %>%
  gt_img_rows(team_wordmark)
```

```{r}
gt_plt_summary(mtcars)
```
